args.title: checkout-api: v2.3.1 failing health checks, rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) since the latest deploy of v2.3.1, with error rate at 18% and service healthy=false.

Action taken: Rolled back checkout-api from v2.3.1 to v2.3.0 in all production regions. v2.3.0 was the most recent release previously healthy in production (v2.2.9 is older; v2.3.1-rc is staging-only and unhealthy).

Note: The first rollback attempt failed with a partial failure (orchestrator error) after completing us-east only, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1. A retry completed the rollout to all three regions.

Current state: All regions on v2.3.0, service healthy=true, error rate down to 0.2%.

Follow-up: Root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures is not yet identified; investigate before any redeploy.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident was created successfully (INC-0001) despite the timeout — no retry needed. Task complete.

## Summary

**Rollback performed:** checkout-api rolled back from **v2.3.1 → v2.3.0** in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west).

- **v2.3.0** was chosen as the most recent release healthy in production. (v2.2.9 is older; v2.3.1-rc is staging-only and itself unhealthy.)
- **A hiccup along the way:** the first rollback attempt returned a partial failure — an orchestrator error halted the rollout after us-east, leaving us-west and eu-west still on the broken v2.3.1. I checked state, retried, and the second attempt completed cleanly across all regions.

**Verification:** Current state is v2.3.0 in all regions, `healthy: true`, error rate down from **18% → 0.2%**.

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001** (SEV2) for checkout-api documenting the failure, the rollback, the partial-failure/retry, and the current healthy state. The initial create call timed out client-side, so I verified via `list_incidents` that it had in fact been created rather than blindly retrying.

**Open follow-up:** Root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures is still unknown — worth investigating before any redeploy of that version.

Rollback then create incident. Rollback first (dependency: incident describes what I did), so sequential.
